rationale: The buyer is real and nameable — engineering managers and platform engineers at companies already paying $20–100+/seat/month for Claude Code or Codex, giving them a clear budget and a ROI pressure to justify spend. However, the core deliverable (multi-session replay, cost attribution, quality scoring across messy real workflows) requires non-trivial instrumentation: capturing session telemetry from Claude Code or Codex APIs, aggregating across engineers, and producing comparable metrics — this isn't a one-week Claude-prompt-plus-Stripe build. Operational autonomy is also capped at 5 because meaningful interpretation of session data likely requires periodic human curation of benchmark definitions and report framing, and early customers will want custom dashboards. Two build_gates fail (buildability_with_ai=5 < 6 required; operational_autonomy=5 < 7 required), so the stage is capped at validate despite the commercial signal.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a 'real-session AI coding ROI report' — a recurring report card showing engineering teams their actual Claude Code / Codex cost, velocity, and quality trends across real messy sessions, not toy benchmarks. To validate without building: the factory drafts a one-page PDF sample report and a 5-question intake survey (team size, tools used, biggest cost concern), posts the Typeform link to HN, r/ExperiencedDevs, and a few engineering Slack communities, and offers the first 5 teams a free manual version in exchange for a $49/month commitment. Outreach (DMs to HN commenters on AI-coding threads, cold emails to eng managers at Series A–C startups visible on LinkedIn) is drafted by the factory and goes out only after Youval approves each batch. If 3+ teams pre-commit, the factory can then design a lightweight data-collection flow — a CLI wrapper or GitHub Action that logs session metadata to a shared bucket — but that integration step means build complexity is genuinely higher than standard Claude+Stripe, so validate first. Ongoing delivery of manual reports requires ~1–2 hours of operator time per customer per month at this stage, which is the honest blocker to autonomy; only invest in automating the pipeline if pre-commitments confirm demand.
notes: Two build_gates unmet: buildability_with_ai=5 (needs session telemetry integration from Claude Code/Codex APIs — not a simple prompt+form build) and operational_autonomy=5 (per-customer report assembly requires human judgment until the data pipeline is built). Validate by seeking 3+ pre-commitments before any build investment. The problem is real and the buyer has money; the question is whether a lightweight automated version is feasible before a well-funded competitor ships it.
